card.name: Partway through split-up words
card.fires_on: The piece of a longer word that comes just before the word's ending, most clearly the 'in' in 'interleukin' before a hyphen and number. Also seen inside place names like Tuscany and in non-English words.

modes.label: Interleukin names
modes.description: The 'in' ending of interleukin right before '-1', '-2', '-6' or '-15'.
modes.example: concurrent use of anakinra (an interleuk<<in>>-1 antagonist) and another TNF

modes.label: Other split words
modes.description: Middle pieces of rarer words such as place names, foreign words or capitalized terms.
modes.example: In 1559 the grand duke of T<<usc>>any, Cosimo I de’ Med
